anchors.quote: when, and only when, the entity becomes party to the contractual provisions of the instrument

claims.supported_statement: Recognise the contractual financial liability when the issuer becomes party; proceeds are assumed equal to instrument fair value.

anchors.quote: measure a financial asset or financial liability at its fair value plus or minus

claims.supported_statement: Initial measurement uses fair value; this slice assumes proceeds equal fair value and no transaction costs.

anchors.quote: fixed number of its own equity instruments in exchange for a fixed amount of cash or another financial asset is an equity instrument.

claims.supported_statement: Fixed-for-fixed equity classification, conditional on ordinary non-puttable shares, functional currency and exclusion of settlement alternatives/contingencies.

anchors.quote: On initial recognition, the fair value of the liability component is the present value of the contractually determined stream of future cash flows

claims.supported_statement: AG31(a): discount liability cash flows at comparable non-convertible market yield; paragraphs 28–32 allocate residual proceeds to equity.

anchors.quote: the equity component is assigned the residual amount after deducting from the fair value of the instrument as a whole

claims.supported_statement: Paragraph 31 supplies residual allocation. Equity is not remeasured; retained on expiry is a local deduction from paragraph 22 and liability-only extinguishment, not a separate quoted redemption rule.

anchors.quote: An entity shall classify all financial liabilities as subsequently measured at amortised cost, except for:

claims.supported_statement: Ordinary liability uses amortised cost. Exclude fair-value designation/trading, derivatives, guarantees, transfer liabilities, below-market commitments and business-combination contingent consideration.

anchors.quote: the allocation and recognition of the interest revenue or interest expense in profit or loss over the relevant period.

claims.supported_statement: Effective-interest method allocates interest expense; use opening liability times the assumed exact annual effective yield.

anchors.quote: minus the principal repayments, plus or minus the cumulative amortisation using the effective interest method

claims.supported_statement: Amortised cost roll-forward follows contractual payments and cumulative effective-interest amortisation.

anchors.quote: when, and only when, it is extinguished – ie when the obligation specified in the contract is discharged or cancelled or expires.

claims.supported_statement: Remove the discharged liability; paragraph 3.3.3 difference is profit/loss. At this exact maturity, consideration equals carrying amount, so zero settlement gain/loss.

anchors.quote: On conversion of a convertible instrument at maturity, the entity derecognises the liability component and recognises it as equity.

claims.supported_statement: AG32: maturity conversion reclassifies liability to equity, leaves original equity within equity and produces no gain/loss.

anchors.quote: financial liabilities measured at amortised cost.

claims.supported_statement: 8(g), read with paragraph 8 lead-in: disclose carrying amounts of financial liabilities at amortised cost on the face or in notes.

anchors.quote: total interest revenue and total interest expense (calculated using the effective interest method)

claims.supported_statement: 20(b): disclose effective-interest totals for liabilities not measured at fair value through profit/loss. This is selected note content only.
